text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Communist Akel party switches tactic for the presidential elections in early 1998. After failing to secure the support of opposition parties for a candidate, it wants a commitment from them that they will support its candidate in a possible second round.
- British forces broadcasting scrambles its television signal in Nicosia.
- A popular beauty spot in the Akamas peninsula is threatened by unlicensed development.
- Credit card spending increased by 47 percent in the first two months of the year.
- Sigma-Severis and Athienitis Securities plan five new initial public offerings.
- The United Nations put emphasis on the adoption of goodwill measures between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides to improve the climate for talks.
- Foreign mediators express caution at the prospects of progress on the Cyprus problem. The inertness of the United States and the political instability in Ankara dampen the prospects.
- String on an anorak strangled a 20-month-old girl in Paphos.

- President Glafcos Clerides is due to meet incumbent Democratic Rally party leader Yiannakis Matsis tomorrow when the latter is due to take a final decision on whether he intends to stand for re-election in the party.
